topic: Gold standard and additional tests for bacterial overgrowth

14C-D-xylose breath test: sensitivity and specificity >90%, more specific than the H2 breath test; a nonradioactive 13C version is suitable for children and pregnant women.

main_section: Diagnostic tests - General tests of absorption
topic: Interpretation details of stool fat, acid steatocrit, lactose H2 breath test, pancreatic tests
candidate: Quantitative fat: borderline 8-14 g/24 hr may occur in secretory or osmotic diarrhea not due to malabsorption; false negatives if fat intake inadequate; false positives with mineral oil laxatives or rectal suppositories (e.g., cocoa butter). Sudan stain: many droplets per 40x field positive; NMR method (normal fat <20%); 90% sensitivity/specificity for >10 g/24 h, drops at 6-10 g/24 h. Acid steatocrit: inexpensive screening test, normal <10%, sensitivity 100%, specificity 95% vs 72-hr quantitative fat. Lactose H2 test: late peak (3-6 hr) >20 ppm suggests lactose malabsorption; other sugars can be tested. Secretin test: duodenal double-lumen tube, measures bicarbonate and enzymes; sensitive but labor intensive and invasive. Fecal elastase-1: equal sensitivity to secretin test for moderate-to-severe insufficiency, more specific than fecal chymotrypsin, unreliable with mild insufficiency, false positives with high stool volume and mucosal disease.
main_coverage: MAIN p93 gives only one-line descriptions; none of these interpretation points (searched steatocrit, chymotrypsin, late peak).
handout_text:
Quantitative stool fat: borderline 8-14 g/24 hr can occur in secretory or osmotic diarrhea not caused by malabsorption; false negative if fat intake is inadequate; false positive with mineral-oil laxatives or rectal suppositories (e.g., cocoa butter).
Acid steatocrit: cheap screening test for fat malabsorption; normal <10%.
Lactose H2 breath test: a LATE peak (3-6 hr) of >20 ppm suggests lactose malabsorption (contrast the EARLY peak within 2 hr in bacterial overgrowth).
Fecal elastase-1: as sensitive as the secretin test for moderate-to-severe pancreatic insufficiency but unreliable in mild insufficiency; false positives with high stool volume and mucosal disease. Secretin test is sensitive but labor intensive and invasive.

topic: Small-bowel biopsy details, permeability studies, SeHCAT interpretation, Schilling test
